# Making the Attack Ring
BEYBLADE TIME!!!
For my Hack Life week two, I decided to make a Beyblade!
I felt nostalgic and decided to go through with that (also, it may have been due to the fact that
I found a really specific tutorial on Onshape for one on YouTube soooo)

So, for starters, here was the link to the video I followed so I could have a glimpse into the master himself!

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WSZ77soLKdg

Making the Attack Ring
I started by making 3 circles on my top plane. I could access my top plane by clicking on N. Then I went to Sketch.

I had to select a sketch plane to choose my tool. I selected the top plane.
And I used the center point circle tool to make my circles well

I gave my circles the following measurements. To change the measurements of my circle, I clicked on the dimensions tool, selected my circles, and placed the appropriate measurements.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/mZKFEMEIAEQ1UpTgazjp9xUySy88SbqC/260ada1be869dc75bcf5f0c825b825906c2cdb3e82bb95945200efd9076d6a50.png)

NOTE THAT MY UNITS WERE IN CENTIMETERS

Then I had to create construction lines. These lines created intersections that sectioned different parts of my Beyblade. It looked like this

Then I needed to define specific angles!
I started by selecting the diagonal line and the center line by just clicking on them like so:

Then I set the angle to 45 degrees and did the same on the other side.

Then, to do the same on the other side using the mirror tool:

I clicked on the horizontal line:

Then I selected each line I wanted copied. It looked like this.

There was no need to set the angles to 45 because the lines were mirrored and thus had the same measurements.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/mZKFEMEIAEQ1UpTgazjp9xUySy88SbqC/9d77fe1f22d33ca92a744cceffaeadf4a7365cc8c239a27d3ad17e2484a62d9e.png)

Then I used the trim tool to get rid of the lines.

Then I extruded it by 0.3cm and rounded inner corners:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/mZKFEMEIAEQ1UpTgazjp9xUySy88SbqC/1d7031c992873f45ccca2fe93e68048242571195a00a4f9bb0205530563636d1.png)

Then I clicked on the extruded face and, using Sketch, started a rectangle from the center. The rectangle measured 0.128 cm.

I added the project tool
between the circle I just created and the edge of my base.

Finally, I used trim to remove the top of the rectangle and the 3 other sides of the circle. Then I used Sketch fillet  to round the corners of my new shape.
I was left with this.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/mZKFEMEIAEQ1UpTgazjp9xUySy88SbqC/f08066d05cfcbc2b2cb6b890e12ee7b1ddde0005fa65208276f0772221dbe6ed.png)

I extruded this at a thickness of 0.1 cm.

Then I needed to hollow out the shape I just made. To do that (STILL WITHIN SKETCH 3), I used Offset and selected these sides.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/mZKFEMEIAEQ1UpTgazjp9xUySy88SbqC/c8010de27c75c598d583c77f6549148f57f5b6d224365dff7186042213ea62a7.png)
I pulled it inward like this.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/mZKFEMEIAEQ1UpTgazjp9xUySy88SbqC/c84434f5e365bea6a579c45f96daf4d607c9a8fb53d92e97aa603af76d6e600a.png)
I made another circle.

I positioned it as so (the tutorial I followed suggested putting a distance of 1.5 mm; instead, I put one of 1.7 (0.17cm) because I thought it was too close.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/mZKFEMEIAEQ1UpTgazjp9xUySy88SbqC/327d3deb4a4b7a908b52f137d92bfe57194d95cd2521254481c6ad908b56d315.png)
Then I selected the innermost side of the shape and the circle I just made to link them closer

Finally, I dragged the small Sketch I made to the circle so that they touched like this.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/mZKFEMEIAEQ1UpTgazjp9xUySy88SbqC/8063e6109f4d8a02e4899888b0816348813e9a218b212f1a7ec2f32be0a9c68c.png) Then used the trim tool to remove the parts of the circle I didnt need.

Then I extruded this shape I had just made to REMOVE. I selected a second ending to extrude on both sides. Finally, I extruded with a thickness of 0.0025cm.

FINALLY, I used the fillet tool to round ONLY the outer corners and the top of the extruded shape.

Then I was done with the attack ring, well half of it !!!

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/mZKFEMEIAEQ1UpTgazjp9xUySy88SbqC/8506550dcf7b48491686de29ae31d930da59cafffbb3dd92315f58b3319a49d2.png)
